title: Automate source-change watcher as a scheduled hash-diff check
context: The M0 watcher-001 is a manually-triggered script. For sustainable maintenance the source-change check must run on a schedule so that license or content drift in allow-listed sources is caught without manual action. This is especially important as the number of schemes and sources grows in M1+. The automation does not auto-update; it flags and alerts, and a human reviews and decides.
objective: Wire the source-change hash-diff check (from watcher-001) into a scheduled CI job (e.g., a GitHub Actions workflow scheduled weekly via cron) that re-fetches each allow-listed source URL, compares hashes, and opens an issue or posts a comment on any CHANGED or UNREACHABLE entry. The maintainer reviews and takes action; the watcher itself never auto-updates.
acceptanceCriteria: .github/workflows/check-sources.yml (or equivalent) runs scripts/check-sources on a weekly schedule (or configurable interval)
On any CHANGED or UNREACHABLE result, the workflow creates a GitHub issue (or posts to an existing tracking issue) listing the affected sources and the hash diff
Workflow exits non-zero only if the fetch/compute step itself errors; hash differences are flagged but do not fail the scheduled run (to avoid alert fatigue on unavoidable upstream changes)
The workflow does NOT auto-update allow-list.yaml; flags only — a maintainer must review and take deliberate action
Workflow is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md or a maintenance README; disable/re-enable instructions included
pnpm build && pnpm lint passes; workflow YAML is syntactically valid
resources: PLAN.md — Security & privacy (supply-chain; automated watcher in M1)
output: .github/workflows/check-sources.yml (scheduled GitHub Actions workflow); updated CONTRIBUTING.md or docs/maintenance.md
